details: was an American company that specialised in text-to-speech (TTS) software for embedded devices, mobile, desktop, and network/server applications. NeoSpeech was founded by two speech engineers, Lin Chase and Yoon Kim, in Fremont, California, US, in 2002. NeoSpeech was privately held, headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Stephen Hawking was briefly a NeoSpeech TTS user in 2004, but soon returned to using his iconic DECtalk voice synthesizer since he identified with it so strongly. Adobe Systems has selected NeoSpeech speech synthesis for their e-learning authoring suite Adobe Captivate.

explainer.lead: NeoSpeech was an American company specializing in text-to-speech software for embedded, mobile, desktop and server applications. It was founded in 2002 by speech engineers Lin Chase and Yoon Kim.

tiers.eli5: It was a company that made computers talk, including briefly giving Stephen Hawking a new voice.
tiers.practitioner: It is relevant as a historical TTS vendor; a notable case is that Stephen Hawking tried its voice in 2004 but returned to his DECtalk synthesizer because he identified with it strongly.
tiers.paperLevel: A privately held company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, founded in Fremont, California, in 2002; the definition provides no technical specification of its synthesis methods.

explainer.example: Hawking briefly used a NeoSpeech voice in 2004 before switching back to his familiar DECtalk voice.
